record.paper_title: Non-Supersymmetric (but) Extreme Black Holes, Scalar Hair and Other Open Problems
record.context_brief: Extreme Kerr entropy in Euclidean semiclassical gravity
record.original_question: For the extreme Kerr black hole, whose angular momentum reaches the extremality condition and whose horizon area is finite, is its entropy nonzero as the horizon-area interpretation suggests, or could the Euclidean semiclassical calculation give a different result?

evidence.quote: What about rotating BHs? Let us go back to N = 1. The extreme limit of the Kerr BH is reached when M = J, before the supersymmetric limit M = 0 is reached (the angular momentum does not appear in the B bound but it does in the extremality bound), but the supersymmetric limit implies the extreme because M = 0 implies J = 0.

The extreme Kerr BH has finite horizon area and usually this is identified with non-vanishing entropy, although it is not clear whether from the Euclidean semiclassical point of view this would be so. The temperature is zero.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider the extreme Kerr black hole, i.e. the Kerr solution of vacuum Einstein gravity with mass $M$ and angular momentum $J$ saturating the extremality bound $M^2 = J$ (in geometric units $G=c=1$), so that the inner and outer horizons coincide, the surface gravity vanishes (Hawking temperature $T=0$), and the horizon area $A$ is finite and equal to $8\pi J$.

The Bekenstein–Hawking area law would assign entropy $S = A/4 = 2\pi J \neq 0$. On the other hand, the Euclidean semiclassical approach computes black hole entropy from the on-shell gravitational action of a regular Euclidean section with periodic imaginary time $\tau \sim \tau + \beta$, $\beta = 1/T$; in the extremal limit this construction degenerates (the would-be conical singularity is absent for any period, the bifurcate Killing horizon disappears, and the Euclidean section has an infinite throat).

Determine the entropy of the extreme Kerr black hole as obtained from a properly defined Euclidean semiclassical gravitational path integral. Specifically, decide whether this entropy equals the horizon-area value $A/4 = 2\pi J$, or whether it vanishes (or takes some other value), and justify the result by a consistent treatment of the Euclidean action and boundary terms for the extremal geometry.
artifact.category_tag: Black hole entropy / Euclidean quantum gravity
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether the extremal Kerr entropy obtained from the Euclidean path integral equals $A/4$ or vanishes has long been controversial. Classic arguments (Hawking–Horowitz–Ross, Teitelboim) suggested $S=0$ for genuinely extremal black holes because the Euclidean topology and period of imaginary time differ from the non-extremal case. More recent work (2023–2025) on near-extremal Kerr thermodynamics, using one-loop Schwarzian/JT-like modes and proper boundary terms, reproduces the area law $S=A/4$ at the saddle point but finds that strict extremality is invalidated by large quantum fluctuations that lift the ground-state degeneracy, so the literal $T=0$ entropy is not simply $A/4$. The status is best described as partially resolved: the semiclassical extremal limit is now well understood as singular, with the area-law entropy emerging only as a near-extremal saddle.

status_evidence.title: From Nonextremal to Extremal: Entropy of Reissner-Nordström and Kerr black holes Revisited
status_evidence.snippet: The absence of a conical singularity in the Euclidean continuation of extremal black holes implies that the periodicity of the Euclidean time remains undetermined. Consequently, the entropy of extremal black holes cannot be uniquely derived using the Euclidean path integral method alone.
status_evidence.claim: Euclidean semiclassical method does not uniquely give A/4 for extremal black holes.

status_evidence.title: One-loop corrections to near extremal Kerr thermodynamics from semiclassical Virasoro blocks
status_evidence.snippet: At sufficiently low temperatures, the semiclassical thermodynamics is invalid; low-temperature fluctuations remove the ground-state degeneracy.
status_evidence.claim: Recent semiclassical analyses show extremal Kerr ground-state degeneracy is lifted, modifying the naive A/4 result.

status_evidence.title: Logarithmic Corrections to Kerr Thermodynamics
status_evidence.snippet: Quantum corrections to Kerr thermodynamics near extremality.
status_evidence.claim: Active recent work on extremal Kerr entropy corrections.
